How to Register a Trademark with the UAE Ministry of Economy (MOEC)

A practical intellectual property masterclass for founders, SaaS companies, and international brands on securing 10-year exclusive trademark protection across all 7 UAE Emirates under Federal Law No. 36 of 2021.

1. Why Register a Trademark in the UAE?

Enacted under Federal Law No. 36 of 2021 on Trademarks, registering your brand name, logo, or slogan with the UAE Ministry of Economy (MOEC) establishes nationwide legal monopoly ownership across Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah, and all Northern Emirates.

In a fast-growing commercial hub like Dubai, holding a registered trademark prevents competitors from registering confusingly similar business names, protects against counterfeit goods, and builds valuable corporate equity for international M&A transactions.

2. Pre-Filing MOEC Trademark Search & Nice Classification

The UAE uses the international Nice Classification system, dividing trademarks into 45 classes (Goods 1–34 and Services 35–45).

Common target classes for modern startups include:

  • Class 42: Software development, SaaS applications, and IT consulting services.
  • Class 35: Advertising, e-commerce retail platforms, and business management services.

Before filing, an official clearance search in the MOEC trademark database must be performed to confirm that no identical or conflicting mark is currently registered.

4. Step-by-Step MOEC Trademark Application Workflow

The trademark filing procedure follows a 5-step legal sequence:

  1. Step 1: Clearance Search: Verify brand name and logo availability across target Nice classes.
  2. Step 2: Portal Submission: Upload brand logo image (JPEG/PNG), trade license, and applicant passport copy.
  3. Step 3: Legal Examination: MOEC examiners check for compliance with public order and existing marks.
  4. Step 4: Public Opposition Gazette: Publish mark in the Official Bulletin for a 30-day public objection period.
  5. Step 5: Certificate Delivery: Pay final registration fees and download the digital 10-Year Trademark Certificate.

5. Government Fee Structure & Madrid Protocol International Expansion

Official MOEC government fees (application fee, publication fee, and final registration certificate issuance) total approximately AED 6,500 to AED 8,500 per class.

Once filed in the UAE, brand owners can leverage their UAE national application as an origin base to extend international trademark protection across 130+ member countries via the WIPO Madrid Protocol system.

6. Brand Enforcement & Customs Protection

Holding a registered MOEC trademark certificate enables brand owners to register their mark with Dubai Customs (IP Rights Department).

Dubai Customs monitors sea and air cargo ports, seizing counterfeit shipments bearing your trademarked logo before they enter the UAE market.
